evidence.interpretation: The subscription effect encloses its own sequential request dispatcher. The run effect races cancellation and finalizes according to outcome; cleanup is not delegated to garbage collection.

The later factory uses a parallel start dispatcher, while each subscription owns sequential controls. Source documentation says each subscription re-runs the stream; the old two-sequential-dispatcher design must not be prescribed for concurrent subscriptions.
The final fixture asserts after the resource use completes, unlike the earlier immediate flag assertion. onSubscribe deliberately does not set the flag. The test is inspected, not executed.

The TCK adapter deliberately returns a publisher after resource release to test failure signalling. Its successful-publisher fixture uses allocated and drops the release action, which is not production ownership guidance.

subscribeStream delegates to the lifetime-enclosing effect; StreamOps.subscribe delegates to subscribeStream. This validates the historical follow-up API, not current availability or Play integration correctness.
This follow-up uses CE3.4.4 and Scala 3.2.1/2.12.17/2.13.10, with a JVM reactiveStreams project depending on coreJVM and Reactive Streams TCK/TestNG test dependencies.

claims.rule: When adapting foreign callbacks, separate ordered protocol control operations from long-running data work, and assign listening-server ownership to the outer Resource rather than an independently restartable inner consumer stream.
claims.applicability: Inference grounded in the CE3.4.0-RC1 Dispatcher migration and a CE3.5 snapshot async_ semantic migration. The reactive-streams JVM adapter and JVM/Native socket source are separate implementations. Preserve the target version's cancellation semantics instead of doing textual async_ replacement. Supplemental #2300/#3341 evidence is contextual discussion only. A synchronous handoff bounds pending elements only if producers respect backpressure; repeated independently dispatched sends can still accumulate.
claims.counterexample: A shared sequential dispatcher that is busy running the subscription cannot also service the request needed to unblock that subscription. Closing a server socket to cancel only an inner accept-stream consumer destroys restartability; using a no-op cancel token can leave real work unowned.

claims.rule: Keep terminal-state checks inside the ordered control effect; enclose per-subscription dispatchers in the subscription lifetime, and distinguish parallel start capacity from sequential control ordering before migrating a foreign publisher.
claims.applicability: Observed reviewer correction and final source in merged January 2023 PR #3107, following #3000. CE3.4.4 Reactive Streams JVM adapter only; current code must rediscover its actual subscribe API. Source inspection establishes explicit ownership, not that every Play/Akka consumer migrated or that garbage collection is sufficient.
claims.counterexample: Checking completed before submitting can race dispatcher shutdown. Blocking cancel with unsafeRunSync is unnecessary for ordered submissions. Copying the TCK fixture allocated._1 into production loses its release action; using one sequential start lane for concurrent long-lived subscriptions prevents progress.
